key_idea: Chords of a convex polygon that share no point form a non-crossing matching, so do interval DP over vertex ranges: vertex i is either unused or matched to some k, splitting the range into two independent parts.
sketch: dp[i][j] = best for vertices in the half-open range [i,j). Transition: dp[i+1][j] (i unused), or for each k in (i,j) with M[i][k]=1: 1 + dp[i+1][k] + dp[k+1][j]. Because the polygon is convex, linearising the circle at vertex 0 loses nothing. O(n^3/6) ~ 2*10^7 operations for n=500, trivial in the 12 s limit. Pitfall: paths sharing an endpoint also conflict, so it is a matching, not just a non-crossing chord set.
